The Commission proposed (via the 'Digital Omnibus on AI' / 'AI Omnibus') to extend the timeline for applying high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, tying application to confirmation that needed standards and tools are available.

The AI Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025, a political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.
As amended by the AI Omnibus (referred to as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027.
The obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) apply from 2 August 2028.

Article 111(2)/113 of the consolidated Regulation states that for high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III (2 August 2026 in the earlier consolidated text, now effectively tied to the new application dates), the Regulation applies only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date.

The 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are described by some commentators as 'backstop dates' that would only take effect automatically if no further amendment occurs; absent agreement before 2 August 2026, the original Annex III obligations would technically apply from that date.

Several secondary/legal-analysis sources, some undated and one dated April 2026, continue to state that Annex III high-risk obligations take effect or become enforceable on 2 August 2026, without reflecting the Omnibus extension.
Providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III must meet requirements in Articles 8–15 and complete a conformity assessment before placing a system on the market.
Annex III lists eight categories of AI use cases that can be classified as high-risk; it does not automatically make all listed systems high-risk.

Transparency obligations under Article 50 and new prohibitions on non-consensual deepfakes/CSAM apply from 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2026 respectively, separate from the Annex III high-risk timeline.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The AI Act as originally adopted set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations (medium confidence), but this has since been superseded by the "AI Omnibus" amendment, which extended the deadline to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk systems embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) (high confidence). Many secondary sources have not yet been updated and still cite the original 2 August 2026 date, creating confusion despite the legal change confirmed by official EU sources.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
The AI Act as originally adopted provided that obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems would apply 24 months after entry into force, corresponding to 2 August 2026 (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). One European Parliament summary instead describes a general 36-month timeline for high-risk obligations, which would point to roughly August 2027 (medium confidence) ([EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence))—a discrepancy likely reflecting imprecise generalization rather than a distinct legal provision.

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed the "Digital Omnibus on AI" (also called the "AI Omnibus") to extend the high-risk application timeline by up to 16 months, conditioning full application on confirmation that necessary harmonised standards and conformity-assessment tools are available (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [Council Press Release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). This proposal was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Council Press Release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [AI Act regulatory framework](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
As amended, the consolidated Regulation now states that obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). For high-risk systems classified as such because they are embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I), obligations apply later, from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

### Grandfathering and Related Transparency Rules
Article 111/113 provides that high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before the relevant application date remain subject to the Regulation only if they undergo significant design changes afterward (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). Separately, Article 50 transparency obligations and new prohibitions on non-consensual deepfakes/CSAM apply from 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2026 respectively—dates independent of the Annex III high-risk timeline (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Multiple secondary/legal-analysis sources—some undated, one dated April 2026—continue to assert that Annex III obligations take effect on 2 August 2026, without reflecting the Omnibus extension (low confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). This directly contradicts official EU guidance confirming the 2 December 2027 date ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). One commentator frames the 2027/2028 dates as conditional "backstop dates" that would only take effect automatically absent further amendment, implying the original 2026 date could technically still apply in some interpretations (low confidence, flagged) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). A low-confidence source describing Article 8–15 conformity assessment obligations lacks corroboration and should be treated cautiously ([Annex III obligations guide](https://ai-act-readiness.example/annex-iii-obligations-guide)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are now fully final law or still subject to confirmation tied to availability of harmonised standards and conformity tools. The precise official EUR-Lex citation for the amending "AI Omnibus" instrument is not confirmed among provided sources. It is also unresolved whether the 2027 date applies uniformly across all Annex III sub-categories, and the exact interaction between the Article 111/113 grandfathering clause and the new dates is not fully detailed.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The AI Act as originally adopted set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations (high confidence), but this has since been superseded by the "AI Omnibus" amendment, which extended the deadline to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk systems embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) (high confidence). Many secondary sources have not yet been updated and still cite the original 2 August 2026 date, creating confusion despite the legal change confirmed by official EU sources.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
The AI Act as originally adopted provided that obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems would apply 24 months after entry into force, corresponding to 2 August 2026 (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). One European Parliament summary instead describes a general 36-month timeline for high-risk obligations, which would point to roughly August 2027 (medium confidence) ([EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence))—a discrepancy likely reflecting imprecise generalization rather than a distinct legal provision.

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed the "Digital Omnibus on AI" (also called the "AI Omnibus") to extend the high-risk application timeline by up to 16 months, conditioning full application on confirmation that necessary harmonised standards and conformity-assessment tools are available (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [Council Press Release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). This proposal was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Council Press Release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [AI Act regulatory framework](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Dates
As amended, the consolidated Regulation now states that obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). For high-risk systems classified as such because they are embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I), obligations apply later, from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

### Grandfathering and Related Transparency Rules
Article 111/113 provides that high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before the relevant application date remain subject to the Regulation only if they undergo significant design changes afterward (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)). Separately, Article 50 transparency obligations and new prohibitions on non-consensual deepfakes/CSAM apply from 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2026 respectively—dates independent of the Annex III high-risk timeline (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Multiple secondary/legal-analysis sources—some undated, one dated April 2026—continue to assert that Annex III obligations take effect on 2 August 2026, without reflecting the Omnibus extension (low confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). This directly contradicts official EU guidance confirming the 2 December 2027 date ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). One commentator frames the 2027/2028 dates as conditional "backstop dates" that would only take effect automatically absent further amendment, implying the original 2026 date could technically still apply in some interpretations (low confidence, flagged) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). A low-confidence source describing Article 8–15 conformity assessment obligations lacks corroboration and should be treated cautiously ([Annex III obligations guide](https://ai-act-readiness.example/annex-iii-obligations-guide)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are now fully final law or still subject to confirmation tied to availability of harmonised standards and conformity tools. The precise official EUR-Lex citation for the amending "AI Omnibus" instrument is not confirmed among provided sources. It is also unresolved whether the 2027 date applies uniformly across all Annex III sub-categories, and the exact interaction between the Article 111/113 grandfathering clause and the new dates is not fully detailed.
